speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how often does the Ministry ensure that schools adhere to the guidelines on setting their Direct School Admission for Secondary Schools (DSA-Sec) criteria and their selection of students; (b) whether there are systems in place to prevent preferential treatment and abuse of the DSA-Sec process; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider a review of the DSA-Sec route for better standardisation and transparency of the selection process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry has received complaints about the Direct School Admission for Secondary Schools (DSA-Sec) route in the last five years; (b) if so, how many complaints have been received; (c) what actions have been taken to address the complaints; and (d) what are the lessons learned and the follow-up actions from these complaints.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Schools have the flexibility to determine their selection and assessment criteria, so that they can select students who will benefit most from the school's development programmes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the same time, schools are required to adhere to the Ministry of Education's (MOE's) selection guidelines and to uphold the key principles of transparency, objectivity, inclusiveness and student-centricity during the selection process.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, schools are required to update and publish their selection criteria on their website before each DSA exercise.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Schools are also required to form selection panels, led by the school leadership team, to evaluate each applicant.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These selection guidelines are reviewed and updated before the start of each year's DSA exercise.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am not making any accusations, to be clear, that there is any kind of corruption going on.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But rather, I think there is a need for transparency behind the DSA process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I wonder whether the Ministry has any plans for a far more thorough review, rather than on a case-by-case basis, of the entire DSA system in its entirety?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But if the Member thinks that there is a problem with the entire system, then, I would also suggest for him to let us know where his areas of concerns are so that we can take a look at this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because, as the Member has suggested, I think there is a difference between anecdotal evidence, where someone says something versus a system problem.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If there are anecdotal incidents, even individual cases where the Member suspects that there is something is not right, he can let us know and we will get to the bottom of it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I make a distinction between isolated cases and what we talk about: the system.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, that is just to put it in context: seven cases out of 4,000.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I will make the following two other points.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, when we look at DSA, we are looking at, essentially, the potential of a child.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are also looking at how the child is able to fit into the school's programme.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Granted that this system will be such that there is some degree of assessment on potential and not just based on current performance.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We would hope that people do not hothouse their children for performance, in lieu of potential.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And we need to understand one step further behind this system.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When we only had the PSLE system to allocate students to school, there were comments and feedback that, perhaps, we were too rigid, too narrow.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The reason for the DSA is to widen the spectrum of talents and abilities with which we assess a child, in order to best site the child in the right place for secondary school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Granted, any system like that will require a level of assessment on the potential of the child and beyond the performance of the child.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I can fully understand that there will be isolated cases where they may not have gotten their choice and there will be questions, perhaps, allegations of unfair practices.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But if there are such things, let us know.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: My assurance to you is that MOE will look at each and every one of these cases thoroughly.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I had received a written reply from the Minister to an oral Parliamentary Question that I had filed on DSA, prior to this.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, I would like to thank the Minister for that reply.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And I have a supplementary question to ask.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While I believe MOE would review the areas of DSA that can be used, is MOE also receptive to the schools giving feedback?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, if certain schools feel that there are some areas that they would like to suggest or nominate for DSA consideration, would MOE also be open to such feedback to look at how they can increase the diversity of areas that can be used for DSA to be admitted into secondary schools?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, many of our schools have proposed to MOE the areas which they would like to focus on, in terms of their DSA selection.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, certain schools have very strong traditions in certain areas.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This may go beyond the sports or arts arena and we allow the school to have that diversity of areas which we want our children to fulfil.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And, as Members know, I have been an advocate that we need to allow a greater diversity of models, a greater diversity in the types of talent that we recognise in our children and to help them fulfil that potential.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That adds to the resilience of our society.
This is the reason why we have allowed our schools to propose ground-up.
But regardless of what you propose, there are certain rules that we hold dear to ourselves in order to make sure that the system is transparent and objective.
I accept that it cannot be done 100% in a matrix because not everything might be able to be captured scientifically, especially when we are talking about the potential of a child.
Someone at a certain age might sprint faster than someone else.
But that does not necessarily correlate to potential.
Because that is how we uphold the integrity of our system.
This process does not stop at Primary 6, because there must be a handover, a handshake, to the secondary school to continue to develop these children whom we have identified.
So, these are the basic core principles that we must adhere to, regardless of the field or the area of DSA that we have allowed the schools to do.
